content.review:
Overall:

My understanding of the method is this:
We take a pre-trained GAN and generate some small number of samples.
We annotate those samples w/ per-pixel annotations.
We then train a model that takes GAN intermediate representations and yields semantic segmentations, so that we can generate a large
dataset of (GAN Sample, Semantic Segmentation) pairs, which can then be used to train a semantic segmentation model.

If you want to train a semantic segmentation model for a large data set of images with no per-pixel annotations,
this could potentially be useful.
However, if you buy this motivating scenario (I think I do, but I don't know much about semantic segmentation),
why couldn't we have taken the labeling budget we spent to label the GAN samples, used it to label
some fraction of the real images, and then use some semi-supervised learning technique on those.
Is the answer 'semi-supervised learning doesn't work yet for segmentation, even though it does seem to be working well for object recognition'?

Regardless, the writing of this paper leaves a lot to be desired.
I think that the authors would have to substantially improve clarity in order for me to reccommend acceptance.
I would like to see other reviewers more familiar with semantic segmentation weigh in as well:
how realistic is this problem setting?
If we found ourselves in this problem setting, would this be a sensible way to solve the problem?
The work would benefit from clarifying those points.

Detailed Comments:
Presumably you did not mean for your title to be 'TEACHING GAN TO GENERATE PER-PIXEL ANNOTATION CONFERENCE SUBMISSIONS'

The introduction is pretty abrupt...

> We propose method for joint image and per-pixel annotation synthesis
*a* method

> We show that separate semantic segmentation network trained on synthetic dataset generalizes on real images.
*a* separate

> The show that GANs lear internal
*they*, *learn*

> Interestingly, training takes a few minutes and Decoder successfully learns on a small number of training examples
Can you be a bit more specific than this?
How few images can you use?
How costly is it to annotate those images.

> After Decoder is trained we can create a large dataset of pairs of GAN-generated images and corresponding masks predicted by Decoder.
At this point in the paper, I don't know why you want to do this?
Presumably to train a segmentation model later, but the paper should read in such a way that
I don't have to guess that.

> sythetic
typo

Minor: table 1 and 2 should have captions that tell you how to read them.
Otherwise readers have to scan the text for the description.


> We test two variants of backbone
This is the first I've seen backbone mentioned.
What is that?

I don't know much about semantic segmentation.
Can you give intuition for why the jump in Intersection over union is bigger than
the jump in accuracy?

For fig 3, why are the first and 3rd examples so dark?
THe top and bottom results look identical for the 2nd and 4th examples,
so the darkness seems important.

content.review:
The paper proposes a method for joint image and per-pixel annotation synthesis with GAN. Join image and per-pixel annotation can be a good idea however the paper needs significant improvement on literature review, model presentation and experiment result to be able to publish in ICLR. Detail comments are as following,

1. On the literature review part. And not only list the GAN papers that published recently ,but show an in depth understanding of these papers. Moreover, the review the works that is relevance to the proposed idea since there exists ton of papers related to GAN.

2. Model presentation part. How the loss function will be changed for this task. Formulate the problem and proposed idea mathematically. Detail explanation of the decoder part will also help.

3. Experiment. Two class problem is trivial task. how will the model perform in much boarder segmentation task? How was the quality of the images generated? How were results compared with other state of art?

content.review:
The paper proposes a method to synthesize the training data for semantic segmentation. The method adds an additional network to GAN-based image generator which annotates pixel masks for targeted features in generated images. Another semantic segmentation network is trained by both the original training data and many synthesized data from the proposed network.

Overall, there is very few information in the main text. Especially, there is no implementation details of the additional decoder, and no explanation about features fed to the decoder. I'd say that it is hard to reproduce the results in this paper.

Some experiments look unfair. E.g., the proposed method additionally uses 20 generated images with human annotations, which means that the proposed method has twice many opportunity to obtain information from human. For fair experiment, these images should also be used to train the baseline systems.

Some experimental results only show its output images without any statistics and/or explanations. It is hard to grasp what is the important information of these results.
